record.paper_title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism. Maxent-Nesom: Concepts, Construction, Application, Open Questions and Criticisms
record.original_question: Can the source term that represents the unavoidable weak interaction between a nonequilibrium system and its surroundings be derived and studied in detail beyond the paper's provisional weak-coupling relaxation-time approximation, while still explaining the infinitesimal source that selects retarded Liouville solutions and introduces irreversible evolution?

evidence.quote: A detailed study is left for a future publication, here suffice it to say that in the weak coupling limit and using some assumptions it can be obtained an expression of the type of a relaxation-time approximation.

In the spirit of this point of view we can then say that in Zubarev's approach to MaxEnt-NESOM the infinitesimal source in Eq. (38), which selects the retarded solutions of the regular Liouville equation and introduces irreversible evolution from an initial condition of preparation of the nonequilibrium system, is a result of the inevitable interaction of the system with the surroundings in the weak coupling limit.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a quantum many-body system S in contact with a much larger thermal-bath-like surroundings B, with total Hamiltonian H = H_S + H_B + λ V, where V couples S and B and λ measures the coupling strength. Let ρ(t) be the statistical operator of the composite system obeying the Liouville–von Neumann equation, and let ρ_S(t) = Tr_B ρ(t) be the reduced operator of S. In the Maximum-Entropy Nonequilibrium Statistical Operator (MaxEnt-NESOM / Zubarev) formalism, one writes a modified Liouville equation for ρ_S of the form

    ∂ρ_S/∂t + (i/ħ)[H_S, ρ_S] = −ε (ρ_S(t) − ρ̄_S(t)),  ε → 0⁺,

where ρ̄_S(t) is an instantaneous "relevant" (generalized Gibbsian) operator built by maximization of the informational entropy subject to constraints on a chosen set of macrovariables, and the infinitesimal source on the right-hand side selects retarded solutions of the Liouville equation and breaks time-reversal symmetry, producing irreversible evolution from an initial preparation.

The question is: can the source term on the right-hand side be derived, starting from the underlying microscopic system–surroundings coupling λV, as a controlled consequence of that interaction, beyond the provisional weak-coupling, relaxation-time-approximation form

    (∂ρ_S/∂t)_coll ≈ −(1/τ)(ρ_S − ρ̄_S),

in such a way that (i) the derivation is valid for arbitrary (not necessarily weak) coupling λ and for general (non-Markovian) memory, (ii) the resulting operator still reproduces the ε → 0⁺ infinitesimal source that selects retarded Liouville solutions, and (iii) the resulting irreversible evolution and the emergence of the arrow of time from the system–surroundings interaction are explicitly characterized? Provide such a derivation, or prove that it cannot be carried out in general, and analyze the structure (memory kernel, positivity, entropy production) of the resulting source operator.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work in the Zubarev NSO literature has extended the treatment of the system–surroundings source term beyond a bare weak-coupling relaxation-time approximation, including derivations of dissipative transport coefficients via Kubo formulas, second-order dissipative relativistic hydrodynamics from the NSO, and reformulations of the infinitesimal source as arising from genuine bath coupling. However, a fully general, microscopically derived form of the source term valid at arbitrary coupling that simultaneously reproduces the ε → 0⁺ retarded selection and an explicit irreversibility mechanism does not appear to be settled; the problem is therefore best characterized as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Source Term of the Non-Equilibrium Statistical Operator
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the source term in Zubarev's NSO method and its derivation from system-bath coupling.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work explicitly revisits and derives the NSO source term from system–surroundings coupling, going beyond the original infinitesimal-source prescription.

status_evidence.title: Relativistic second-order dissipative hydrodynamics from Zubarev’s non-equilibrium statistical operator
status_evidence.snippet: Transport coefficients can be obtained at weak coupling via relaxation-time approximation or method of moments, or at arbitrary coupling through Kubo formulas.
status_evidence.claim: The NESOM framework has been pushed beyond weak-coupling relaxation-time approximations using Kubo-type formulas, partially addressing the question.

status_evidence.title: Reworking Zubarev’s Approach to Nonequilibrium Quantum Statistical Mechanics
status_evidence.snippet: Reformulation of Zubarev's approach addressing the role of the infinitesimal source and irreversibility.
status_evidence.claim: The interpretation of the infinitesimal source as a consequence of system-bath interaction has been further developed.
